paper.title: Reward, Addiction, and Emotion Regulation Systems Associated With Rejection in Love

claims.text: Romantic rejection activates the ventral tegmental area (VTA) bilaterally, suggesting that mesolimbic reward/survival systems are involved in romantic passion regardless of whether one is happily or unhappily in love.
claims.evidence: Activation specific to the image of the beloved occurred in areas associated with gains and losses, craving and emotion regulation and included the ventral tegmental area (VTA) bilaterally

claims.text: Activation of brain areas involved in cocaine addiction may help explain the obsessive behaviors associated with rejection in love.
claims.evidence: Activation of areas involved in cocaine addiction may help explain the obsessive behaviors associated with rejection in love.

claims.text: Early-stage romantic love is a goal-oriented motivational state rather than an emotion that uses subcortical mammalian reward/survival systems.
claims.evidence: we used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to study 10 women and 7 men who were happily in love and concluded that it was a goal-oriented motivational state (rather than an emotion)

claims.text: In a study of individuals rejected by a romantic partner within the past 8 weeks, 40% experienced clinically measurable depression, with 12% displaying moderate to severe depression.
claims.evidence: In a study of 114 men and women who had been rejected by a partner within the past 8 wk, 40% experienced clinically measurable depression; of these, 12% displayed moderate to severe depression

claims.text: Romantic love is a universal or near-universal human phenomenon, with evidence found in 147 of 166 societies surveyed.
claims.evidence: In a survey of 166 societies, Jankowiak and Fischer (1998) found evidence of romantic love in 147 of them.

claims.text: Romantic love shares behavioral characteristics with addiction including intensely focused attention, mood swings, craving, obsession, compulsion, distortion of reality, emotional dependence, and loss of self-control.
claims.evidence: Several psychologists regard romantic love as an addiction because it shows addiction characteristics such as the lover's intensely focused attention on a preferred individual, mood swings, craving, obsession

claims.text: All participants in the rejection study reported thinking about their rejecting partner 85% of their waking hours and yearned for the rejecter to return to them.
claims.evidence: All participants responded that they thought about their rejecter 85% of their waking hours. All participants also reported that they yearned for the rejecter to return to them

claims.text: Romantic rejection activates brain areas associated with gains and losses, craving, and emotion regulation, including the ventral striatum, medial and lateral orbitofrontal/prefrontal cortex, and cingulate gyrus.
